items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: We had Nick Turner, another bass record.

ctx.x: So you got a real close song, didn't you?

That was the first bass song. And then when we went up a little further, when we added Geechee Robinson, another drum roll. We had Nick Turner, another bass record. I had Jimmy Johnson on the string bass. And I had Nick Turner on the Suze for MWM on the drum roll. And then later on I added Harold Holmes, who's now in Canada, who did most of my arranging. And as we traveled over the country, I added here, subtracted, added and subtracted.
And I found the change in the years. Did you ever play any other state fairs? You want to start it by now or is it?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Two string basses and Nick on the tuba.

ctx.x: I've listened to him awful hard and I've never even noticed. Well, I can't. No, you can't hardly hear him. Well, Nick was a real soft man. Mm-hmm. I see. Must have been one of the first bands, one of the first, to use two basses, I guess.

First band, they used three basses. You had three basses? Two string basses and Nick on the tuba. Who were the string basses? Uh, old man, uh, Jimmy Johnson. Uh-huh. Uh, Harold Holmes. And Nick Turner. Where? First band to use the word swing.
You're talking about America's Greatest Swing Band. America's Greatest Swing Band. Well, how would those billings read? What would it say then?
